decision_conditions: <div style="text-align: justify;">The proposal would result in the additional residential flats being sited on garden land. As such, the principle of the development is contrary to the Harrow Core Strategy of directing new residential and other development to the Harrow and Wealdstone Opportunity Area, town centres and, in suburban areas, to strategic previously developed sites and would therefore harm its implementation, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies CS1.A and CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Garden Land Development (2013).</div>

<p style="text-align: justify; ">The proposal, by reason of the poor and cramped layout of the ground floor flats, poor outlook to living spaces for each flat, and lack of family bathroom provision would result in a poor standard of living accommodation for future occupiers of those flats, to the detriment of their residential amenities and an overdevelopment of the site, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D6 and D3, (D.7 and D.10) of The London Plan (2021), Policies DM1 and DM26 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), The Mayor of London Housing Supplementary Planning Guidance (2016), the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010) and Housing Design Standards LPG (2023).&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align: justify; ">The proposed conversion of the dwellinghouse into four flats and the sub-division of the rear garden into four separate amenity areas, would result in an overly intensive use of the site and a poor standard of living accommodation, to the detriment of the living conditions of the potential future occupiers of the flats and the character and appearance of the property and the area, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies D3 D (7) and (11) and D6 of The London Plan (2021), policies DM1, DM26 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align: justify; ">The proposed two storey side and rear extension, by reason of its excessive width would give rise to a disproportionate new semi-detached addition which would fail to respect the proportions and subsume the host dwelling, it would also fail to provide a coherent pattern of development in the street scene thus would substantially harm the form, openness and proportion of the site, relationship with the properties in the locality accentuated by its prominent siting to the detriment of the character and appearance of the streetscene and the pattern of development within the surrounding area and would therefore be contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3.D(1) and D3.D(11) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS.1B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013) and the Adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).</p>

<p style="text-align: justify; ">Insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that the proposed development would result in no adverse increase in flood risk or would manage and reduce the surface water runoff, contrary to contrary to policies SI 12 and SI 13 of the London Plan (2021) and DM9 and DM10 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).&nbsp;</p>
description: Conversion of HMO into four self contained flats (3 X 2 bed and 1 X 1 bed); two storey side to rear extension; single storey rear extension; alterations to roof to raise ridge height and rear dormer; front porch; external alterations; separate amenity space; bin and cycle stores
